title: November 2026: the GUI shootout, again
model: Claude Opus 5.5 (high effort), one agent per toolkit, in OpenCode

toolkits.name: WebUI (reference)
toolkits.summary: The reference app every toolkit was compared against, shown in Chromium with the first-launch setup dialog.

shots.caption: The reference WebUI at 1280×800 with the first-launch setup dialog

toolkits.name: Flutter
toolkits.myNotes: Near pixel match in every state shown: setup dialog, Settings with exit-127 tab (action-exit), library confirm, dark Microarray and mirrored Hebrew (rtl-he). Only nit is tighter, heavier page-title tracking; Windows shots are equally faithful.
toolkits.summary: Close to pixel-level with the reference, with every page, data source, action and setup step working.
toolkits.lessons: Fonts were the main fight: the Linux engine ignores fontconfig aliases, so the agent loads Chromium's faces itself. dart:io cannot create process groups, so cancel uses setsid plus a watchdog.

toolkits.name: Compose Desktop
toolkits.myNotes: Indistinguishable from the reference across main, Settings exit-127, Library, dark VCF and a fully mirrored Arabic page (rtl-ar). Arabic text renders slightly small, which is the only visible difference; Windows shots match too.
toolkits.summary: Every control is hand-made from Compose foundation primitives styled after the reference CSS, so the window is close to pixel-for-pixel.
toolkits.lessons: Material looks nothing like the reference and AWT cannot pick folders on Linux, so controls are custom and the picker shells out to zenity. The JVM tax shows in startup, memory and a 187 MB distributable.

toolkits.name: wxPython
toolkits.myNotes: Layout, RTL Arabic settings and the exit-127 terminal are faithful, but buttons, selects and Retry are GTK-native gradients and the setup dialog in main.png sits on a visible light square shadow. There is no dark-theme shot; the Windows shots are close.
toolkits.summary: Native GTK entries, choices and file choosers sit inside custom-drawn chrome, very close to the reference.
toolkits.lessons: There are no Linux wxPython wheels, so it runs from a ~1 GB conda-forge environment, and a GLX probing hang under a fresh Xvfb needed a bundled Mesa. wx itself was the easy part.

toolkits.name: Qt 6 / QML
toolkits.myNotes: Faithful in every state: setup dialog, Library actions, dark Microarray, mirrored Arabic (rtl-arabic) and streaming setup. Field labels sit a pixel or two high, nothing more; Windows shots match.
toolkits.summary: A C++ backend with a compiled-in QML front end; the full workflow works and the screenshots are almost identical to the reference.
toolkits.lessons: Qt Quick fit the app well. CSS grid sizing, native select popups and Chromium's font fallbacks had to be approximated, and without a SIGTERM handler killed apps orphaned their child processes.

toolkits.name: GTK4 / libadwaita (Rust)
toolkits.myNotes: Layout, dark theme and mirrored Arabic are faithful, but every shot carries GTK client-side window chrome (min/max/close) and Inter instead of the reference font. The setup dialog in main.png is libadwaita-styled, with centred text and a blue Run Setup button.
toolkits.summary: Native GTK 4 and libadwaita covering the whole workflow, close to the reference with deliberate native touches such as Adwaita dialogs and header-bar controls.
toolkits.lessons: Rebuilding the page on every change loses focus, so widgets get stable names to restore it, and Rc/RefCell re-entrancy needs care. Without a window manager, RTL windows land off-screen.

toolkits.name: Slint
toolkits.myNotes: Main, dark Settings, dropdown, tooltip, confirm and Library table are near-identical. rtl.png is only partly mirrored: Load Bundle and the Main tab stay left, the action buttons run in reverse order and BAM is left-aligned.
toolkits.summary: Every page renders through custom Slint components tuned against the reference CSS; the main window is very close to the reference.
toolkits.lessons: Slint cannot create widgets at runtime, so every control shape is declared up front and chosen by kind. Bindings break once the user types, and there is no RTL layout direction.

toolkits.lessons: No blockers, since the wheels bundle Qt. Qt has no CSS grid or flex-wrap, so it needed a custom flow layout, and controls update in place because re-rendering loses focus.

toolkits.name: Toga / BeeWare
toolkits.myNotes: Layout and dark FASTQ are close, but the setup dialog has square corners and no shadow, checkboxes are GTK switches (Microarray, Annotate) and sidebar icons sit above the text. In rtl.png the page title and section header stay on the left.
toolkits.summary: Toga's GTK 3 backend renders the whole workflow very close to the reference, with one app-wide GTK stylesheet and a few native escape hatches doing the styling.
toolkits.lessons: Toga's Pack layout has no borders, radii, tooltips, label wrapping or checkbox, so text is pre-broken with Pango and switches stand in for checkboxes. Modal dialogs are faked with a second window.

toolkits.name: Textual
toolkits.myNotes: Remarkably faithful structure for a terminal (scrim, dialog, Library table, dark theme), but the monospace cell grid has one text size, the app icon is pixelated in main.png and the settings steps are a flat list. arabic.png reverses word order.
toolkits.summary: A terminal UI with the reference's layout, colours and full workflow, shown in a vendored kitty terminal that also draws the real bundle icon.
toolkits.lessons: A TUI is a monospace cell grid, so there is no large title and controls are flat one-row fields. Shipping it as a window means vendoring a terminal, and Textual has no native dialogs or RTL.

toolkits.name: GPUI
toolkits.myNotes: Near-identical main, dark Microarray, confirm, streaming and failure states. In rtl-ar.png the Choose buttons sit between field and label and final yā' loses its dots in a few words.
toolkits.summary: Zed's GPUI, through gpui-kit and gpui-component, renders the whole workflow within a pixel or two of the reference, including dialog shadows, focus rings, RTL and a dark theme.
toolkits.lessons: Picking a crate is the hard part: the crates.io gpui is old, so it builds on gpui-kit, a recent Zed snapshot whose API shifts between releases. It pulls in ~800 dependencies for a 43 MB binary, and file dialogs work only through xdg-desktop-portal.

linux.build: 9 min 27 s first clean build (-j4, ~600 crates); ~26 s app-only rebuild
linux.note: Ready time measured on a busy machine; 213–225 ms earlier on a quieter one. Built with gpui-kit (a recent Zed snapshot).

windows.notes: Warm median of 5 on the busy shared VM; single .exe, DX11 on WARP; Arabic/Hebrew needed a ~40-line patch to GPUI's Windows text layout (vendored).

toolkits.name: Makepad
toolkits.myNotes: LTR pages and dialogs match closely, but icons sit visibly high in the sidebar and buttons, and the Library confirm has no shadow. locale-ar.png is not mirrored at all (left-aligned Arabic with doubled line spacing), and there is no dark theme.
toolkits.summary: Pages are built at runtime by a custom widget that instantiates Makepad's live-DSL templates from the bundle JSON; the main window is very close to the reference and nearly the whole workflow works.
toolkits.lessons: Makepad's DSL is static, so a dynamic widget tree needed custom code, and two text bugs (word wrap, RTL scripts) had to be fixed in a vendored, patched makepad-draw. There are no native file dialogs, RTL layout or dark theme.

toolkits.name: Dioxus Native (Blitz)
toolkits.mayNote: May's Dioxus was a WebUI webview shell; this is native Blitz rendering
toolkits.myNotes: Near-identical main, dropdown, typed confirm, dark Info/BAM and mirrored Arabic. Sidebar and section icons sit a few pixels high and the play triangles are larger than the reference's.
toolkits.summary: dioxus-native: Blitz lays out real HTML and CSS and draws it with Vello's hybrid renderer on wgpu, with no webview or browser engine, so the reference's design ported almost directly. (May's Dioxus entry was a WebUI webview shell.)
toolkits.lessons: Blitz has no select, placeholder or title tooltips yet, so those are components, and it fires only input events, not change. A spawn dies with its component, so long-lived work needs spawn_forever; Xvfb needs a vendored lavapipe.

toolkits.name: Xilem / Vello
toolkits.myNotes: Every shown state (main, Library, Settings, streaming, mirrored Arabic) is near-identical to the reference. No dark-theme or exit-127 shot.
toolkits.summary: Xilem and Masonry from git main, drawn by Vello on wgpu, render the whole workflow very close to the reference, a big step from May's near-empty window.
toolkits.lessons: The crates.io release is a year behind, so it builds on git main; the light look is a full re-theme, and the dropdown, tooltip and log views had to be written by hand. Masonry has no RTL, and wrapped text is sometimes measured as one line.

linux.build: 36 min 41 s clean release (-j2) at load average 20–30; a few minutes on an idle machine

toolkits.name: Moonframe
toolkits.myNotes: Recognisable layout, but with a different (Lucide-style) icon set, larger type, spinner-style selects, a 'Loaded settings…' debug line in every terminal and no dark theme. In rtl-ar.png only the sidebar moves: banner, title and the truncated description stay left-aligned.
toolkits.summary: The whole window is Luau mods on Moonframe's GPUI renderer, fed by Rust providers for the bundle, processes and terminal; it matches the reference closely in layout and light theme.
toolkits.lessons: Luau live reload made iteration fast: after a handful of Rust builds, every layout and style change was a Luau edit and a recapture in seconds. GPUI needed a vendored lavapipe to run under Xvfb, and the library owns the command line and the terminal, so both needed workarounds.

linux.build: 18 min clean release (-j2, no lease); ~10 s incremental; Luau changes need no rebuild
linux.note: Ready time measured at load ~7 (~740 ms on a quieter run). Size includes 15 MB of vendored lavapipe, needed only under Xvfb.

windows.notes: Warm median of 5; GPUI on DX11/WARP; same GPUI Windows RTL text patch as the GPUI port; app declares DPI awareness itself.

toolkits.name: Zenbu UI
toolkits.myNotes: Close in main, dark FASTQ, Library, Microarray and Hebrew RTL, but Inter replaces the reference font and the play icons sit high. demo.png has lost its Load Bundle toolbar, and RTL labels are not bold.
toolkits.summary: A native X11/GL window on Zenbu, a private C immediate-mode UI stack, rendering the whole WGS Extract workflow close to the reference with light and dark themes and right-to-left mirroring.
toolkits.lessons: As a private monorepo with no packaged release, Zenbu had to be built from a mirrored scratch workspace with the app overlaid. Its core is fast and its bidi text just works, but form-level widgets, RTL mirroring and wake-ups on child output were all hand-built, and images draw as black boxes under software GL.

toolkits.name: Qt Widgets
toolkits.myNotes: Faithful main, dark Info/BAM, Library, streaming and setup states. In rtl-arabic.png the sidebar FASTQ and VCF labels are left-aligned and the Arabic description line spacing is loose; cards stop short of the scrollbar.
toolkits.summary: Classic Qt 6 Widgets in C++20 (no QML, no webview) laid out to match the reference, with the whole WGS Extract workflow and RTL working, in a 1.1 MB binary.
toolkits.lessons: QSS fights you: its min-height overrides fixed sizes, it has no line-height, and the gtk3 platform theme forces its own fonts. Widgets don't re-render on their own, so small host containers rebuild only the data-driven parts to keep focus.

toolkits.name: Dear ImGui (C++)
toolkits.myNotes: Faithful layout across many states (dark Library, typed confirm, data sources, exit 127), but main.png shows a visible grey square shadow behind the modal. Error text and paths wrap or overflow mid-word (main, rtl-arabic), and text is slightly soft.

toolkits.lessons: Immediate mode has no look-and-feel layer, so every widget is drawn by hand; font sizes needed CSS em scaling, and RTL needed FriBidi because ImGui has no bidi or shaping. There is no accessibility tree and no native file dialog.

toolkits.name: Raygui (C)
toolkits.myNotes: Indistinguishable from the reference in main, dark FASTQ, Library table, dropdown, typed confirm and failure tooltip, with a fully mirrored, correctly shaped Arabic Settings page (locale-ar). Only nit: the warning icon touches the error text.
toolkits.summary: About 6,600 lines of hand-written C11 on raylib 5.5, with raygui used only for text boxes and buttons: cards, tables, popups, tooltips, anti-aliased shapes and RTL mirroring are all custom, and it closely matches the reference.
toolkits.lessons: raygui covers little of this app (no layout, cards, tables, popup selects or icon fonts), and without reliable MSAA under Xvfb rounded shapes and shadows had to be nine-patch textures. Text was the hardest part, RTL needed a mirroring layer, and there is no accessibility support.

linux.build: 50 s clean (2 jobs, including the vendored raylib)
linux.note: Size is a 1.6 MB statically linked binary plus 1.7 MB of fonts. RSS is mostly llvmpipe software GL under Xvfb.

toolkits.name: React Native (desktop)
toolkits.myNotes: Faithful Linux layout, but with Inter, taller text fields, a setup dialog without a shadow, and in rtl-ar.png a left-aligned description and error with an inverted terminal tab strip; no dark shot. Windows has mismatched sidebar icons (VCF eye, Annotate check) and a raw PowerShell error dump.
toolkits.summary: One ~5,000-line TypeScript React Native codebase on two renderers: on Linux react-native-gtkx 0.4 draws RN's components as real GTK4 widgets (it implements RN's components and APIs, not Meta's runtime), and on Windows react-native-windows 0.85 runs Fabric and Hermes. May's version never showed a UI; this one hit the same blank window on Windows until a Metro resolver bug was fixed.
toolkits.lessons: Writing the app was quick because it is plain React Native; the platform layers took the time, with four gtkx workarounds on Linux and six toolchain and config problems on Windows. Windows has no Node, so files, processes and pickers come from a ~450-line C++ native module.

linux.build: 33 s clean build.sh (GIR codegen and vite, 2 cores; npm ci not included); 10 s rebuild
linux.note: Ready is the median of 5 warm runs (1.4–2.4 s). RSS (426,800 kB) is Node, V8 and GTK. Size is dist/ only; Node 26 (144 MB) and the system GTK 4.24 are not counted.

windows.notes: Warm median of 5; 3.96 s first launch; includes Windows App SDK.
